ai_summary: This document is a press release reporting money market operations data as of May 15, 2026, not a regulatory circular requiring summarization. It provides operational statistics including overnight and term segment volumes, RBI liquidity facility operations, and scheduled bank cash reserve positions, with the weighted average call money rate at 4.87% and net liquidity absorbed of ₹2,48,221.57 crore across outstanding operations. The data reflects RBI's management of system liquidity through various instruments including repo operations, standing deposit facilities, and the standing liquidity facility, with scheduled commercial banks maintaining cash balances of ₹7,64,826.03 crore against an average daily reserve requirement of ₹7,87,838 crore for the fortnight ending May 15, 2026.

The RBI Amendment Directions, 2026 establish a new Chapter V-E requiring commercial banks to provide continuous banking services in calamity-affected areas through temporary premises (with RBI approval), satellite offices, mobile facilities, and restored ATM services within 30 days. Banks may open simplified "small accounts" for calamity-displaced persons lacking identification documents and may waive or reduce fees/charges for affected customers for up to one year. These provisions become effective July 1, 2026, enhancing financial inclusion and accessibility during natural disasters or declared calamities.

These Directions establish mandatory financial reporting standards for Payments Banks in India, requiring them to prepare Balance Sheets and Profit & Loss Accounts in formats specified under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, with strict compliance to Accounting Standards notified under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021, subject to RBI guidelines. The Directions cover detailed requirements for presentation and disclosure of financial statements, including capital structure, reserves, consolidated statements, and specific provisions for inter-branch accounting, nostro account reconciliation, fraud provisioning, and deferred tax treatment. Payments Banks must implement these directives with immediate effect and ensure that mere mention of activities in compilation instructions does not imply regulatory permission, requiring reference to extant statutory and regulatory requirements for permissibility determinations.

ai_summary: The RBI Directions, 2025 consolidate credit facility regulations for five All India Financial Institutions (EXIM Bank, NABARD, SIDBI, NHB, and NaBFID), establishing comprehensive prudential norms for digital lending, project finance, and non-fund-based credit facilities. Key requirements include mandatory board-approved policies, specific conduct and customer protection standards for digital lending arrangements, and detailed prudential conditions for project finance disbursement and monitoring. The Directions apply immediately upon issuance and establish regulatory safeguards to ensure orderly growth, financial stability, and protection of depositors' and borrowers' interests while encouraging innovation in credit products and delivery mechanisms.

# RBI Circular Summary: All India Financial Institutions – Responsible Business Conduct Directions, 2025

The RBI has issued mandatory Directions applicable to five AIFIs (EXIM Bank, NABARD, SIDBI, NHB, and NaBFID) establishing a comprehensive framework for responsible lending conduct, requiring Board-approved policies on Fair Practices Code, grievance redressal mechanisms, and penal charges. Key requirements include full transparency in loan disclosures (processing fees, pre-payment charges, penalties, conversion charges), displaying "all-in cost" on websites, written communication of loan rejection reasons, and verification of applications within reasonable timeframes. AIFIs must ensure non-discriminatory charges, proper credit appraisal independent of collateral substitution, and implement grievance redressal mechanisms with dispute resolution at next higher levels, with periodic Board reviews of compliance and mechanism functioning.

RBI's 2026 Directions mandate commercial banks to implement the Basel III Standardised Approach for calculating risk-weighted assets and capital requirements for credit risk, effective April 1, 2027. The framework establishes specific risk weights for various exposure classes (sovereigns, corporates, retail, real estate, NPAs, etc.) and incorporates external credit ratings from eligible agencies for determining capital adequacy. Banks must comply with enhanced due diligence requirements, credit risk mitigation principles, and apply standardised methodology for securitisation exposures to ensure prudent and comparable risk assessment across the banking system.

Rural Co-operative Banks must become members of all RBI-registered Credit Information Companies (CICs) and report credit information using standardized Uniform Credit Reporting Format (UCRF) with membership fees capped at ₹10,000 one-time and ₹5,000 annually per CIC. The directions establish a comprehensive framework for credit information reporting, dissemination, data quality standards, customer grievance redressal, and compensation mechanisms to ensure confidentiality, security, and consumer protection. These directions came into immediate effect from November 28, 2025, and apply to all State and Central Co-operative Banks operating as rural credit institutions.

ai_summary: These RBI Directions, 2025, establish comprehensive regulatory framework for Local Area Banks' branch authorization and outlet operations, covering banking outlets, Business Facilitators/Correspondents, doorstep banking, and ATM/CDM deployment with strict governance requirements. LABs must obtain Board-approved policies for opening banking outlets, which must operate minimum four hours daily for five days weekly with proper signage, monitoring mechanisms, and grievance redressal systems. The Directions define various banking service delivery models including Administrative Offices, Back Offices, and specialized outlets, while mandating banks to report outlet information to RBI and ensure transparent operations with appropriate risk management, particularly for doorstep and correspondent-based banking services.

The RBI's 2025 Directions establish comprehensive guidelines for Small Finance Banks on classifying investments into four categories (HTM, AFS, FVTPL/HFT, and Associates/Joint Ventures), with specific requirements for initial recognition, subsequent measurement, and fair value determination based on market activity and security type. Banks must establish investment policy frameworks approved by their Boards, implement robust internal controls, maintain Investment Fluctuation Reserves, and follow prescribed income recognition and non-performing investment provisioning standards. These Directions, effective immediately, replace previous investment portfolio guidelines and require banks to comply with detailed operational, accounting, and reporting requirements while ensuring all investment activities remain permissible under existing statutory and regulatory frameworks.

# RBI KYC Directions for NBFCs - Summary

These Master Directions, effective from their RBI website publication, establish comprehensive Know Your Customer (KYC), Anti-Money Laundering (AML), and Countering Terrorist Financing (CFT) requirements for all Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) with customer interfaces, aligned with India's FATF commitments and the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002. The Directions cover customer acceptance policies, risk management, customer identification procedures, due diligence, record management, and reporting obligations to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India, with additional requirements for NBFC branches and subsidiaries operating abroad to comply with the more stringent of local or RBI regulations. Non-compliance frameworks and detailed procedural requirements across eleven chapters govern NBFCs' obligations to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing while maintaining financial system integrity.
